concerns.text: The plan states 'Scale/Scope: ~500-2000 HEA compositions' and 'handle <500 samples gracefully'. For a regression task with 5 predictors plus interaction terms (implied by tree models) and 1000 bootstrap resamples, a sample size of N=500 yields extremely low statistical power to detect anything but massive effect sizes. The plan lacks a power analysis justification for this sample size relative to the intended R² claims (SC-001). Without this, the study risks being underpowered to validate the research question.

The plan claims to address 'VII. Statistical Rigor' by including VIF and permutation tests. However, it does not specify how the 'multiple-comparison correction' (FR-007) will be applied to the permutation p-values specifically. Permutation tests generate a null distribution; applying Bonferroni/BH to these p-values requires a clear definition of the 'family' of tests (e.g., per descriptor, per model, or global). The plan is vague on the exact statistical procedure for correcting the permutation p-values, risking invalid inference.

The plan mentions 'Stratified 80/20 hold-out test set'. Stratification requires a categorical target or a meaningful binning of the continuous target (yield strength). The plan does not define the stratification bins for the continuous yield strength variable. Arbitrary binning can introduce bias or reduce effective sample size in folds, compromising the validity of the hold-out evaluation (FR-005).
